project: NBA Live 97 PS1 decompilation and native port

features.name: Trade players
features.notes: Windows two-team screen, swaps/transfers, Help/View/Compare, native saves/discard and Reset are implemented and tested. Exact original timing, rendering and waveform acceptance remain open. See docs/trade_rosters_workflow.md.

features.name: Sign free agent
features.notes: Windows 100-slot free-agent list, destination validation, signing, child routes, native saves and preserved re-entry undo behavior are implemented. Bounded accounting does not establish full transitive or presentation fidelity. See docs/sign_free_agent_progress.md.

features.name: Release player
features.notes: Native release/refusal, Help/View/Compare, save/discard/restart and Reset paths have functional acceptance. Original animation/audio fidelity remains open; partial describes the full feature, not an absent screen. See docs/release_players_progress.md.

features.name: Reset rosters
features.notes: Native confirmation, default-roster restoration, failure-safe persistence and restart are tested. This is bounded frontend behavior, not complete PS1 card or all-mode equivalence. See docs/reset_rosters_progress.md.

features.name: Re-order rosters
features.notes: Windows original-asset screen, selection/swap, Help/View/Compare, native saves/discard and Reset are implemented and tested. The older instruction ledger's pending slice labels are not current host status; full original-reference acceptance remains open. See docs/reorder_rosters_workflow.md.

features.name: Create player
features.notes: 40-slot durable catalogue, manager/Edit/New/Delete, 32-field editor and articulated original-data preview are native-tested. Roster insertion/resolution and final original raster/whole-screen acceptance remain open. See docs/create_player_progress.md.

features.name: Frontend music decoding and host routing
features.notes: Five-track bank and recovered router use native finite audio output. Verification is scoped to decoding/routing and host regressions, not exact SPU timing, every transition/pause caller or full-match playback. See docs/music_playback_workflow.md.

features.name: Original sound startup and sample ownership
features.notes: Recovered startup, SPU heap/transfer, interrupt and event owners compose in native tests. Natural host startup, timer cadence, voice synthesis and complete resource ownership remain open. Registration does not establish callback scheduling. See docs/audio_startup_workflow.md.

features.name: Team selection
features.notes: Exhibition Team Select and User Setup are connected to the Windows frontend and bounded accepted-match snapshot. Season/playoff/special-team handoff, full original-reference acceptance and gameplay launch remain open. See docs/team_select_workflow.md.

features.name: Starting lineup flow
features.notes: Lineup recovery, player binding, role and controller owners compose in isolated period tests. The complete live starting-lineup/substitution flow is not connected. See docs/match_runtime_workflow.md.

features.name: Match loading
features.notes: Windows accepts an ordinary-exhibition snapshot; separate native resource and period composition tests exist. Natural loader/entry provenance and a playable match launch remain incomplete. See docs/match_snapshot_workflow.md and docs/match_runtime_workflow.md.

features.name: Native court and player rendering
features.notes: Recovered body/texture/text owners and native CPU/VRAM storage have bounded tests. No playable court or complete match rasterizer/scene is connected; Create Player's preview is a separate frontend path. See docs/game_render_backend_workflow.md.

features.name: Playable basketball controls
features.notes: Recovered input-edge and player helpers have isolated tests, but no host controls operate a live basketball possession. See docs/match_input_edges_workflow.md.

features.name: Match rules and clock
features.notes: Frontend rule settings and bounded period initialization are tested. Live clocks, scoring, fouls, violations and complete period/end behavior remain unimplemented. See docs/match_runtime_workflow.md.

features.name: Native C++ window and main loop

instruction_semantics.method: tiered original-MIPS structural accounting; tiers are never combined

block_classifications.summary: Team/palette selection, address calculation, and the 160-entry PS1 CLUT copy are replaced by local mixed-palette decoding plus validated native RGBA loading.
The original two palette snapshots and counters initialized to 16 are represented by retained source/target teams and a native factor progressing from 0 through 16 at 17 ms per frontend tick.
MIPS prologue/epilogue and the signed team bound are represented by a value-returning native function with explicit safe rejection outside team IDs 0..28.
The fixed fifteen-slot address arithmetic, -1/null branch, ordinary FUN_8005FE14 lookup, result store, and loop are represented by the fixed-size ResolvedTeamSlots traversal and native player index.
The global special-mode check, regular-stat-index-zero test, and FUN_8005768C replacement call are represented by the recovered position/rating-tier calculation over the local-only 5x5 FALL table.
The MIPS prologue, global-context fetch, private source-table base, and zeroed loop counters are replaced by native fixed-size containers initialized by the local pack loader.
The nested 29-by-15 signed-short copy and per-team FUN_8005770C call are represented by copySlotTable's fixed team traversal and resolved_team_slots_ assignment.
The second exact 100-short copy loop is represented by the private FREE pack section and fixed free_agent_slots_ container, including 67 IDs and 33 trailing -1 holes.

FUN_80054CBC's roster-owner/count refresh is represented directly, while the +0x72E reset and FUN_8005DB34 call boundary become an explicit derived-rating dirty request. FUN_8005DB34 internals are not claimed here.
Raw roster-table pointer derivation becomes retained team identity plus database injection; the six-iteration descriptor-default copy becomes an explicit six-element reset on every construction.
Default layer 2/limit 3 and the active-special condition selecting global layer+3 are represented by RosterViewerConstructionContext and tested across both branch outcomes.

Descriptor count/index/pointer ownership, global viewer ownership, controller phase reset, paired object flags, and FUN_80039D88 object construction are represented as typed viewer state with the exact recovered binding constants.
The saved-player -1 check/reset and the two saved selection mirrors are represented by typed persistent state normalized before construction.
Saved team 29 is replaced with the active team in mode 2 and team 3 otherwise, with ordinary teams retained, exactly matching both original branches.

FUN_800590B8 construction plus FUN_8003D930 state-0x10 input/draw invocation become explicit constructor, input-state, cancel-sentinel, and callback-bound native state; generic input internals remain separately scoped.
The non-0x100 player/window/team writeback, 0x100 suppression, epilogue, and returned loop result are represented by finishRun, commit/cancel snapshots, and retained result/exit status.

The L2/forward direction branch, inclusive active-layer wrap loop, conditional layer-4 skip, selected-layer writeback, and redraw of layer-label object 0x1B are explicit native state transitions; the label call is not audio.
FUN_800594F0's descriptor extent result drives the primary animation reset, followed by an exact visible-row refresh count.
Layout 0x23 conditionally resets the secondary group when the descriptor extent changes and refreshes its visible rows on every layer change.
Controller page save, temporary zero, layout rebuild, exact restoration, stat-window reset, and return are retained.
The special descriptor-29 lock, input-latch clear, previous/forward branch, exact count boundary, and bidirectional slot wrap are explicit typed transitions.
The new slot resolves through the fixed roster table and mirrors the selected player ID into the active frontend page.
The two-frame transition and FUN_80059808 call boundary retain page-dependent headers, visible-row refresh, state-0x24 cool-fact stop/rebuild, and unchanged stat scroll.
Both the successful refresh path and blocked special-roster path return with their exact mutation status retained for verification.

Private archive requests, exact manager initialization, descriptor bindings, layout/layer selection, selected player context, cool-fact choices, and 24-entry descriptor setup are explicit native lifecycle state.
The four-entry initialization loop is retained as exact zero column starts paired with step value two, followed by both -1 fact sentinels.
Controller 0x39 binding, frontend state 0x11, state -1 input loop, distinct draw/action callbacks, scheduled teardown, and final frontend -1 restoration are independently testable.

methodology_notes: Function progress measures the original PS1 binaries and never infers completion from native screens.
A partial function is evidence coverage, not a completed original function.
Native-port milestones are manually maintained status counts, not a game-completion percentage or estimate of remaining effort.
The milestone catalogue is incomplete and items differ substantially in scope. Partial has no numeric credit; verified means marked verified in the manifest, not exhaustive proof.
Instruction-semantic tracking reports source ownership, block accounting, CFG verification, runtime trace equivalence, and exact matching as separate tiers.
Inventories cover five known disc programs, including both loader overlays and GAMEONLY; automatic function discovery is not proof that every entry point or reachable resource is known.
Function identity includes the binary: shared numeric addresses and duplicated SDK routines in mutually exclusive overlays are separate inventory records.
Matching means instruction-identical PS1 output; the native C/C++ build cannot satisfy that status.
